info.title: FetchX API
info.description:
FetchX gets any public URL and returns its data. POST /v1/fetch does the work, and POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next gets the page after one. POST /v1/batches takes up to 1000 URLs in one job and runs them at the pace each site can take, with results sent to a webhook or read page by page. POST /v1/estimate says what a request or a batch would cost and take before you send it; the other endpoints read results, download files, list, delete and report credits. A browser request with capture records the page's own network calls, read with GET /v1/fetch/{id}/network or as a HAR file. POST /v1/logins saves a site’s username and password (encrypted, never returned): when a page asks for a sign-in on that site, FetchX signs in by itself and keeps the session for later requests. POST /v1/browser-sessions starts a browser you drive yourself with Playwright, held to the hosts you allow: FetchX sees every request its pages and frames make first and refuses what is off the list. GET /v1/me says which project and key are calling, and the key's own credit limits per day and month and expiry, set in the console. POST /v1/feedback tells FetchX how it handled a page, for example blocked through FetchX but fine from your own connection, so routes can be tuned with real cases. GET /v1/status and GET /v1/prices need no key: the service's state, and what each step costs with the trial credits a new account gets.

Two status layers: the HTTP code says whether FetchX accepted the call; the `status` field says what happened to the fetch. A fetch that ran and failed is HTTP 200 with `status: failed`. A pending fetch is HTTP 202. A 4xx means the request itself was wrong, nothing was sent to the site and nothing was charged.

Billing: a request is charged only when it succeeds, at the price of the step that got the data (plus the page text read, when it asks for `extract`). Failed, uncertain and refused requests cost nothing, and so does a page that loads without what `expect` asked for or without a required `extract` field. Every result says what it cost in `credits`, with a breakdown.

Changes are listed at https://fetchx.ai/changelog (info.version is the latest release). A deprecated route carries Deprecation, Sunset and Link headers until its sunset date; a retired route answers 410 with error.code route_retired and error.details.replacement; an unknown route answers 404 with error.code route_not_found and links to the docs, the changelog and the status page. While maintenance pauses the API, every route except GET /v1/status answers 503 with error.code maintenance, a Retry-After header and error.details.status_url (https://fetchx.ai/status).

post.description:
Gets the page after request {id}'s, as a new request with its own id. Request {id} must have succeeded with a `data.next_page`, and its content must not have expired (7 days) or been deleted.

FetchX builds the new request from the earlier one: the same headers, formats, country, render, wait_for and scroll, plus the cookies the site set on the earlier page. When the earlier page came through a residential browser session, the next page uses the same session (exit IP and device identity) while it is still available, so the site sees the same visitor. For `link`, FetchX fetches the next page's address with the earlier page as referrer. For `click` and `scroll`, it opens the list again, repeats the steps back to the earlier page, then clicks its next control or scrolls further, so each later page of a long list takes a little longer. The new page has its own `data.next_page`, so a list is read by calling this with each new id in turn.

Billed like any request: only when it succeeds, at the price of the step that got the data (a browser step when the next page needs one). A failed next page costs nothing.

post.description: What one request, or a batch of up to 1000, would cost and how long it would take, before anything is sent, reserved or charged. Send the body you would send to POST /v1/fetch, or a batch body ({items, defaults}: each item a URL or a request, merged over defaults). For each request FetchX plans the steps it would try and prices them with what recent requests to the same site took (the step that got the data, its traffic, captcha solves and time: learned from every customer's requests by host name only), its price table, your max_credits and your balance. credits.typical is what one success usually costs and credits.high a high-end cost (90th percentile); credits.expected counts only the share of requests that usually succeed, since failures are free; credits.hold is what the request reserves while it runs. basis says where the figures come from: history (this site's recent requests), routes (a route known to work, priced from other sites), defaults (no history: typical figures for the first step) or assumed. A batch's seconds assume FetchX's per-site pace. notes say what to change when a request would be refused or is likely to fail.

post.summary: Submit many URLs in one job
post.description:
Queues up to 1000 items and answers at once with the batch. FetchX starts the items itself, per site, at the pace it knows each site can take (from what it has learned about the site across all customers: a site that has refused or rate-limited FetchX before gets fewer requests at once, further apart), so you need no pacing or polling loop of your own. Different sites run side by side, within your project's limit of requests at once (one slot is always left for single requests).

Each item is an ordinary request: it reserves credits only when it starts, is charged only if it succeeds, at the price of the step that got the data, and its result is at GET /v1/fetch/{request_id}. Results go to `webhook_url` as each item finishes and when the batch ends; GET /v1/batches/{id}/items pages through them if you poll instead. A batch whose credits run out pauses, and starts again by itself once the balance covers its next item.

post.description: Starts a browser (Camoufox, a hardened Firefox) that you drive yourself with Playwright, and answers once you can connect to it, usually within seconds. Connect to ws_url with playwright.firefox.connect and the API key in the Authorization header, and drive browser.contexts[0]. FetchX holds the session to allow_hosts: every request a page or a frame makes (cross-origin frames included) reaches FetchX's own handler before any route you add, and one to a host off the list is refused and listed in blocked_requests; workers' requests and WebSockets go through FetchX's proxy, which opens connections only to hosts on the list. Saved logins and secrets are typed with POST /v1/browser-sessions/{id}/fill, so they never reach your client. The session closes when you DELETE it, at ttl_s, when your client is idle or gone for idle_ttl_s, or at its traffic limit; FetchX never records what the pages show or what is typed. Billing: the session's price is held when it starts and charged once when it ends (plus residential traffic past the included MB), whatever the reason it closed, except when its browser failed (close_reason error), which costs nothing. Feature id browser_sessions.

scroll.description: How far a page opened in a browser is scrolled before it is read. auto (the default): once the page has filled in, keep scrolling while scrolling loads more, up to 10 screens. off: read the page once it has filled in, without scrolling. A number from 1 to 50: scroll up to that many screens, stopping early at the end of the page; implies a browser, and more screens take more time (raise timeout_ms for many). Scrolling has no fee of its own, but what a scrolled page loads is traffic like any other: on a residential route it counts toward the per-MB charge beyond the included traffic, so off is the cheapest choice when the first screen is enough. A number past 10 reserves credits for 2.5 MB more traffic a screen while the request runs; only what the page used is charged.

country.description: Required for datacenter and residential; null for direct.

render.description: true uses a browser on this route.

formats.description: What to return. body: the response as received (the rendered page after a browser), the default when formats is left out. markdown, text, links and metadata are derived from it (for data from a page, see extract); skeleton: the shape of a JSON body (keys, types, array lengths and a small sample), a few KB instead of the whole body, null when the body is not JSON; screenshot needs a browser. Ask only for what you use: a rendered page can be megabytes of HTML. The body is stored either way and can be downloaded from /v1/fetch/{id}/content.

block_resources.description: In a browser, do not download images, video, audio or web fonts on the page. They carry none of the text but a good part of a rendered page’s traffic, and residential traffic past the included megabytes is charged per MB; the text and every image URL stay in the page. Captcha widgets still load theirs. On a site whose bot protection has walled FetchX, and on any attempt after a wall, the browser loads everything anyway, since a bot check can notice an image or font that never loads. Defaults to true, or false when formats has screenshot.

expect.description: What the page must show to be the content you want. Every condition given must hold, or the step is not a success: auto mode tries a browser, then one fresh IP, and a request that never gets it fails with content_missing and is not charged. A browser waits up to 10 s for the selector after the page settles. A real 404 or 410 is the site’s answer and is not checked.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match at least one element (HTML only).

text.description: Text that must appear in the page’s visible text (or a non-HTML body), ignoring case and spacing.

min_markdown_length.description: The page’s markdown (a non-HTML body’s text) must have at least this many characters.

extract.description: Read the page into JSON. schema is a small JSON Schema whose descriptions say what each field is: a root object asks for one record (a product, an article), a root array of objects (with a description of one record) asks for every record of that kind on a list page. Fields: string (format date, date-time or uri), number, integer, boolean, enum of strings, and arrays of strings or numbers; up to 30 per record. Every value is checked against the page: one the page does not show is null, never guessed. A field listed in required that the page does not show is treated like a missed expect: FetchX tries a browser, then a fresh IP, and a request that never gets it fails with content_missing and is not charged. Costs `extract` credits per started 25,000 tokens (about 100,000 characters) of page text read, up to 150,000 tokens, on top of the step; see credits.breakdown. Only page text is sent to the models, never your headers or cookies. If extraction is unavailable, the request is refused with 503 extract_unavailable before anything is fetched. A next page reads its page with the same extract. Not with HEAD.

schema.description: type object (one record) or array (items: an object, description required, maxItems up to 200). additionalProperties may only be false. At most 16 KB.

instructions.description: Optional context for every field, for example which of several prices to take.

max_attempts.description: The most attempts that may reach the site. Steps refused before anything is sent do not count.

fix_headers.description: Replace automation User-Agents (curl, python-requests…) with a browser one and add a missing Accept and Accept-Language.

max_credits.description: The most this request may cost. Steps that would cost more are skipped.

timeout_ms.description: Total time for all attempts. A captcha solve can take up to a minute, so the default leaves room for one; a synchronous call still answers 202 after 60 seconds if the request is not finished. Up to 180000, or 300000 with actions.

async.description: true answers 202 at once; false waits up to 60 seconds, then answers 202.

webhook_url.description: A public https URL that receives the result when the request finishes.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body returns the same result and is charged once. Generated when absent.

tags.description: Your labels, to filter the list.

capture.description: Record the page's own network calls (its documents, XHR and fetch requests) while a browser renders it, and keep them with the result for as long as its other content (7 days). Read them with GET /v1/fetch/{id}/network, /v1/fetch/{id}/network/{index} and /v1/fetch/{id}/network.har. true records with the defaults; false or null records nothing. capture needs a browser, so with render: auto it makes the request render, and it is refused (invalid_request, details.field capture) with render: never, a method other than GET, or a route whose render is false. Free: it adds nothing to the price. When several browsers are tried, the calls are the last browser attempt's, also when the request fails.

redirect.description: follow: follow redirects (up to 5, each hop checked); data.redirects lists them. manual: answer with the redirect itself, for a login that answers 302 with its cookies: data.status_code is the 3xx, data.final_url the request URL and data.location where it points, and the cookies it set are in data.cookies. Manual is HTTP only: auto mode uses no browser, and render always, route.render, wait_for, screenshot, a number of screens and capture are refused (invalid_request, field redirect).

all_headers.description: Return the response's headers as sent in data.raw_headers: in order, with duplicates (each Set-Cookie) and, over HTTP, the site's own casing.

actions.description: Steps for a browser to take, in order, once the page has loaded (its load event, at most 10 s): wait, click, fill, press, select, scroll, navigate, evaluate a script, wait for a response and more. They run in one tab, in one page and one JavaScript realm: what an evaluate leaves on window stays for later actions until the page navigates. Selectors are Playwright CSS and reach into open shadow roots. Actions imply a browser: method must be GET, render must not be never, redirect must not be manual, a route's render defaults to true (false is refused), and a number of screens to scroll is refused (use a scroll action). Only the browser steps of auto mode are used, and a route runs one attempt. The page is not scrolled or read further after the last action: data.body is its DOM then, data.final_url its address and data.status_code the last top-level document's status. expect and extract read that page. A popup or new tab is closed. Billed as one browser step, with nothing per action; a request whose action failed is free. At most 512 KB as JSON in all.

action_timeout_ms.description: Only with actions: the timeout_ms of every action that does not give its own.

allow_hosts.description: The only hosts the request may reach: exact hostnames, or *.suffix for every subdomain of suffix (not suffix itself). The URL's host must be on the list (else 400 url_not_allowed, field url). In a browser it covers every request and connection the page makes (navigations, frames, scripts, XHR and fetch, WebSockets, workers, redirect hops): one to a host off the list is refused before it leaves FetchX and listed in data.blocked_requests by origin. Over HTTP a redirect to a host off the list is not followed: the 3xx is the answer, with data.location. Captcha widgets load from their vendors' hosts, which are off most lists. A navigate action to a host off the list is refused (400, field actions[i].url).

allow_passive_subresources.description: Only with allow_hosts: let the page load scripts, styles, fonts and images from hosts off the list (GET only, sent without Cookie or Authorization), listed in data.passive_offlist_hosts. Documents, frames, XHR and fetch, WebSockets, beacons, form posts and workers stay on the list.

login.description: A saved login (POST /v1/logins). Left out: the project’s login for the request’s registrable domain, when it has exactly one, signs in when a page asks for a sign-in on a host it covers, and its saved session goes with the request. A login id names the one to use, for example for a sign-in on another domain; false never signs in. Ignored when the request sends its own Cookie or Authorization header. Once FetchX has sent the login on a page, the request makes no further attempts, so a password is never sent twice.

value.description: The secret, 4 characters to 4096 bytes. FetchX never stores, logs or returns it: it is held in memory while the request runs, and wherever a page shows or echoes it (as typed, URL-encoded, form-encoded, JSON-escaped or base64) it comes back as [REDACTED:<name>].

origins.description: The https origins (scheme, host and port, no path), such as https://login.example.com, the secret may be typed into or sent to. Each host must be in allow_hosts.

secrets.description: Secrets for this request only, by name (1 to 8): a password or token FetchX types or sends without keeping it. A fill_secret action types one into a field whose frame is at one of its origins (else the action fails with secret_origin_mismatch). Over HTTP, {{secret.<name>}} in body or a header value is replaced when it is sent (form-encoded in an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body, JSON-escaped in a JSON one); the URL's origin must be one of the secret's, a redirect that would carry it to another origin is not followed, and a GET or HEAD with placeholders needs render: never. While a secret is loaded, anything the page sends that carries it to another origin is stopped, and the request fails with secret_egress_blocked. Once a secret has been typed or sent, FetchX makes no further attempt, on any route. Needs allow_hosts. Refused with 400 secret_not_allowed_here (error.details.field) together with a screenshot, extract, capture.unmask or webhook_url, and in batches. Implies store: false. secrets_used on the result names those that were used. Feature id secrets.

store.description: false: FetchX keeps nothing of the page or of what you sent beyond the response. The first read of the finished result with its body (the 200 answer, or a poll of GET /v1/fetch/{id}) returns the content in full, with the body always inline, and deletes it; unread content is deleted 15 minutes after the request finished. From then on the result keeps only its summary for 90 days (status, page_status, credits, error, attempts, secrets_used) with data null, and the content, screenshot and network routes and the next page answer 410 not_stored. The kept request has no headers, body or action values. Always false with secrets.

NextPageRequest.description: What may change for a next page. Everything else (headers, formats, country, render, wait_for, block_resources) comes from the earlier request, and the cookies the site set on the earlier page are sent with it. An empty object is fine.

scroll.description: As in FetchRequest; defaults to the earlier request's. For a next page that loads as the page is scrolled (next_page.how is scroll), it is how many more screens to scroll past where the earlier page ended (auto: up to 10 more); off is refused there.

expect.description: As in POST /v1/fetch. Left out, the earlier request's expect applies; null drops it, for a list whose later pages do not show what the first one did.

selector.description: A CSS selector that must match at least one element (HTML only).

text.description: Text that must appear in the page’s visible text (or a non-HTML body), ignoring case and spacing.

min_markdown_length.description: The page’s markdown (a non-HTML body’s text) must have at least this many characters.

max_credits.description: The most this page may cost. Not taken from the earlier request: without it, the page may use any step, like a new request. A next page holds credits for the deepest page's traffic (150 MB) while it runs and is charged only for what it used; max_credits caps both.

timeout_ms.description: As in FetchRequest; defaults to the earlier request's. A next page reached by clicking or scrolling opens the list again and repeats the earlier steps first, so deep pages of a long list may need more time.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body returns the same result and is charged once. Generated when absent.

capture.description: As in the fetch request. Left out, the earlier request's capture applies; false or null turns it off. The calls carry this page's number in `page`, so a client can compare page 1's and page 2's calls.

page_status.description: What the page was. content: the page you asked for (with expect, it showed what you expected). not_found: the site’s real 404 or 410, billed like content. empty: it loaded but showed next to nothing, or not what expect asked for. challenge: a bot wall, block or rate limit stopped it (see challenge). login_required: the site asked for a sign-in, and FetchX had no saved login for it or the site did not accept the one it had (error login_required or login_failed). error: anything else (see error). Null while pending.

data.description: What the site answered: on success the real answer, on failure the last response. Null only when nothing reached the site.

challenge.description: The walls the request met on its way, or null when it met none.

credits.description: What this request cost. Present on every result: a pending or failed request shows 0.

charged.description: 0 unless the request succeeded. Never more than max.

max.description: The most this request could have cost: max_credits, or the dearest step it might use (null for unmetered projects).

balance.description: Credits the project has available as this answer is made (null for unmetered projects). Also at GET /v1/balance.

breakdown.description: How the price of the step that got the data adds up; null unless the request succeeded.

attempts.description: One entry per step tried, in order. Providers are never named.

skipped.description: Steps that were not tried, and why.

batch.description: The batch this request is an item of (POST /v1/batches), or null.

index.description: The item's place in the batch's items, from 0.

network.description: Only on requests made with capture: the network capture (null while pending). Top level, not under data, because a request that failed before any page answered still has its capture.

secrets_used.description: Only on a request made with secrets: the names of those FetchX typed (fill_secret) or sent (a placeholder), sorted by name. Values never appear anywhere.

Challenge.description: Blocks, bot challenges and rate limits met on the way, and on the page that answered (a captcha, a wall that cleared). FetchX handles them itself; this says what it met and how it got past.

vendor.description: The bot-protection vendor last seen (datadome, cloudflare, akamai, imperva, human, aws_waf, kasada, or the captcha provider when nothing else names one: arkose, recaptcha, hcaptcha, mtcaptcha), named from the wall page, its headers and cookies, also when the wall came as a rate limit (429); null when nothing said.

passed.description: Whether FetchX got past them to the page.

passed_by.description: rotation: a later attempt on another route or a fresh IP got through; captcha: solved on the page (10 credits); wait: it cleared by itself. Null when not passed.

CreditBreakdown.description: charged = step_credits + captcha_credits + traffic_credits + extract_credits, capped at max.

captcha_credits.description: For a captcha solved on the page, else 0.

traffic_mb.description: Megabytes (10^6 bytes) the step moved, to one decimal.

included_mb.description: Traffic included in a residential step’s price; null when traffic is not charged.

traffic_credits.description: Per started MB past included_mb, on residential steps. block_resources keeps it down.

extract_tokens.description: Page text the models read for extract, in tokens of 4 characters; null without extract.

extract_credits.description: For extract: per started 25,000 tokens of page text read (at least one), up to 150,000 tokens; else 0.

rendered.description: True when a browser produced the result.

content_expired.description: True after 7 days or DELETE: everything below is gone.

cookies.description: Cookies the site set, for multi-step flows: those for the final URL, then those a redirect hop set for another host or path. Over HTTP each cookie a hop wrote says which (hop, 0 for the first response, see redirects); the last write per name, domain and path wins, and a cookie a hop expired is left out.

redirects.description: Over HTTP: the redirects followed, in order, each with the URL that answered, its status, where it pointed and the names of the cookies it set. Empty when the first response was the answer. Not on browser results.

location.description: With redirect: manual, when the answer is a redirect: its Location, resolved against the request URL (null when it is not a URL).

raw_headers.description: With all_headers: the response's headers as [name, value] pairs, in the order sent, with duplicates (each Set-Cookie). Over HTTP the site's casing is kept; a browser reports names lowercased. At most 200 pairs, values cut at 8 KB.

actions.description: With actions: one entry per action, in order (null when the step that answered never got to them).

blocked_requests.description: With allow_hosts: what was refused for being off the list, at most 100, each origin and type once per action.

passive_offlist_hosts.description: With allow_passive_subresources, on a browser step: the origins off the list the page loaded scripts, styles, fonts or images from.

next_page.description: On successful results: how the page leads on, or null when FetchX found no next page. Gone with the rest of the content after 7 days or DELETE.

body.description: The body: utf-8 text, or base64 for binary. Only when formats has body (the default); left out on reads with include_body=false, and when it is too large to inline (see body_url).

body_url.description: Where to download a body too large to inline.

skeleton.description: With formats: skeleton, the shape of a JSON body; null when the body is not JSON.

extract.description: The JSON read from the page for the request's extract: an object for a one-record schema (fields the page does not show are null), an array of records for a list schema. null when the site answered 404 or 410. Only on requests with extract.

screenshot.description: formats: screenshot, base64 JPEG. Also at /v1/fetch/{id}/screenshot.

PageInfo.description: Where this page sits in a list read page by page, and how far it was scrolled.

number.description: 1 for a request made with POST /v1/fetch; each next page adds 1.

previous_id.description: The request this one is the next page of; null for page 1.

screens.description: Screens scrolled reading this page (for a next page that loads on scroll, past where the earlier page ended). 0 when it was not scrolled.

end.description: true: scrolling reached the end of the page and nothing more loaded. false: scrolling stopped (screens or time) while there was more. null: not scrolled.

NextPage.description: How a page leads on to the next one. Open it with POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next.

how.description: link: a link to the next page (url). click: a Next or Load more control the page handles itself, with no address of its own. scroll: the list loads more as it is scrolled further, and scrolling stopped before its end.

url.description: For link: the next page's address.

hop.description: Over HTTP: the response that set it, 0 for the first (see redirects). Left out for a cookie FetchX already had.

rotation.description: A fresh residential IP for the same step.

result.description: not_admitted means nothing reached the site on this step (for example the provider refused the host); it does not count as an attempt. content_missing means the page loaded without what expect asked for.

code.description: The underlying error, when result is not_admitted or failed.

challenge.description: On a blocked or rate-limited step, the bot-protection vendor whose wall it was, when known (for example datadome, cloudflare, akamai, imperva, human, aws_waf, kasada; or arkose, recaptcha, hcaptcha, mtcaptcha when only its captcha says).

missing.description: On a content_missing step, the expect conditions the page did not meet, and extract:<field> for each required extract field it did not show.

wire_bytes.description: Bytes this step moved over the network, requests and responses together. On a residential route this is the traffic billed past the included megabytes.

captcha.description: Captchas met on this step, as type:outcome. passed: the page let the visitor through; still_challenged: the same captcha came back; still_blocked: the captcha went away but the site kept refusing; other outcomes say why no solve was made (for example captcha_timeout). Only a request that succeeds is charged for its captchas.

warmup.description: Browser steps on sites that have refused FetchX before start at the site's home page. passed: it loaded; cleared: a bot check there cleared by itself; solved: the check there was a captcha, which was solved, and the visit went on (see captcha); challenged: the check stayed, so this step ended there and the next one used a fresh IP; failed: the home page did not load, and the page was visited directly.

wall.description: A bot check on the page itself: whether it cleared by itself before any captcha was solved.

content.description: Browser steps on pages that answered: settled when the page had stopped filling itself in (results, listings loaded by script) before it was read; still_loading when FetchX's wait ran out first, so the page may be missing content that loads late. Pass wait_for with a selector for what you need to wait longer.

sign_in.description: A sign-in on the page with a saved login: passed (signed in), rejected (the sign-in form came back), code_required (it asked for a one-time code), failed (no clear answer), no_login (the page asked for a sign-in on a host no usable saved login covers).

secrets_used.description: true on the attempt that typed or sent one of the request's secrets. No attempt follows it.

reason.description: For example excluded_by_provider_rule, over_max_credits or cooling.

action_index.description: action_failed: the action that failed (data.actions[i].error says why).

next.description: What to do next. A request key replays its first result, failures included, so a retry always needs a new idempotency_key.

retry_after_seconds.description: The earliest time a retry can help.

retry_with_new_key.description: true: the same request may succeed if sent again with a new idempotency_key (after retry_after_seconds when given). false: sent again unchanged it would fail the same way; change it as action says.

secrets_used.description: Only on a request made with secrets: the names of those that were typed or sent.

credits.description: Available now: what new requests can reserve. Null for an unmetered project.

reserved.description: Held by running requests; released or charged when they finish.

purchased.description: Credits bought. They do not expire.

payment_hold.description: True while spending is paused over a payment issue.

usd_per_credit.description: What one credit costs in USD: the list price per credit of the pack this project bought last (whichever currency it paid in), or of the smallest pack when it has bought none. Trial and granted credits are not counted. Null for an unmetered project.

EstimateRequest.description: One POST /v1/fetch body, or a batch body: items (URLs, or requests with url) merged over defaults. async, webhook_url and idempotency_key are set once for a batch, never in defaults or an item.

items.description: URLs, or POST /v1/fetch bodies (with url) merged over defaults.

defaults.description: POST /v1/fetch fields every item gets unless it sets its own (not url, async, webhook_url or idempotency_key).

expected.description: typical times the share of requests that usually succeed (failures are free).

high.description: A high-end cost for a success (90th percentile of traffic, with a captcha if the site sometimes needs one).

hold.description: Items only: what the request reserves while it runs (released when it settles).

code.description: no_history, likely_needs_more_credits, likely_needs_other_options, max_credits_too_low, insufficient_credits, balance_may_run_out, balance_limits_pace (a batch), cooling_down, low_success_rate, no_route or extract_priced_by_text (the request has extract).

message.description: What it means and what to change.

index.description: The request's position (0 for a single request).

basis.description: Where the figures come from; none when no step is open to this request.

samples.description: Recent requests to this host the figures are based on.

step.description: The step most likely to get the data.

steps.description: The steps likely to get the data, with their share.

planned.description: The steps FetchX would try, in order.

success_rate.description: Share of recent requests to this host that succeeded; null without history.

error.description: Why POST /v1/fetch (or the batch) would refuse this request; it is left out of the totals.

estimated.description: Requests that would be accepted and are in the totals.

credits.description: Credits available now; null for a project that is not metered.

hosts.description: Batches only: per site, its requests, FetchX's pace for it and its credits.

status.description: The worst state of any component.

notices.description: Scheduled and active notices, then those resolved in the last 14 days.

version.description: The API's version (the latest changelog release).

pause_api.description: While active, the API answers 503 maintenance.

ExtractReport.description: How the page was read for extract. On a failed request, why its page did not give the JSON.

status.description: complete: every required field was found. missing_required: a required field was not on the page (the step was content_missing). unavailable: the models could not run. skipped: the site answered 404 or 410, so nothing was read.

reason.description: For unavailable or skipped: why (budget_exhausted, calls_exhausted, error, not_found...).

page_tokens.description: Page text the models read, in tokens of 4 characters.

truncated.description: True when the page was longer than extraction reads (150,000 tokens), or the call cap or deadline stopped it; fields not reached are null.

records.description: Records returned for a list schema; null for one record.

dropped.description: List blocks left out: empty, repeated, or missing a required field.

source.description: List schema: records read one by one from the page's repeated blocks, or the whole list read at once.

fill.description: List schema: the share of records with each field found.

missing.description: One record: the fields that are null.

reasons.description: Why each missing field is null: not_found (the page does not show it), unsure (the models disagreed or were not confident), ungrounded (a value was read that is not on the page).

evidence.description: The page text the value was read from.

fields.description: One record: for each value found, how sure the model was and where on the page it was.

required_missing.description: The required fields the page did not show.

BatchRequest.description: Many URLs in one job. Each item is a URL, or a POST /v1/fetch body without async, webhook_url and idempotency_key (the batch owns those, and an item that sets one is refused); its fields are laid over `defaults` (a shallow merge: an item's field replaces the default whole). FetchX checks every item before anything is queued: one bad item refuses the batch with 400 naming it (`items[3].formats`, or `defaults.formats` when the default is at fault).

items.description: Up to 1000 URLs, or POST /v1/fetch bodies without async, webhook_url and idempotency_key. Each item’s fields are laid over `defaults`; its result is a request of its own.

defaults.description: POST /v1/fetch fields every item uses unless it sets its own: anything but url, async, webhook_url and idempotency_key. max_credits here caps each item, not the batch.

webhook_url.description: A public https URL. FetchX POSTs each item's result as it finishes (event fetch.finished, the FetchResult without its body, with `batch`), and the batch when it ends (batch.finished) or pauses (batch.paused). The X-FetchX-Event header names the event.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body returns the same batch and queues nothing new. Generated when absent.

tags.description: Your labels for the batch. Items keep their own `tags`.

status.description: running: items are queued or running. paused: the balance does not cover the next item (or spending is on hold), its items ask for extract and extraction is unavailable for now, or the key that submitted it has used its credit limit (paused_reason says which); it starts again by itself once that clears. finished: every item has finished. canceled: you canceled it; items that were running still finish.

paused_reason.description: Why the batch is paused: insufficient_credits or payment_hold until the balance covers the next item; extract_unavailable when its items ask for extract and FetchX cannot read pages into JSON right now (it tries again by itself after 5 minutes; nothing is charged meanwhile); key_limit_reached when the API key that submitted it has used its credit limit for the day or month (it starts again by itself when the limit resets).

finished_at.description: When the last item finished (or the batch was canceled with nothing running).

items.description: Items by status. queued: waiting for its site's pace. running: being fetched. succeeded and failed: as the request's status. canceled: never started.

charged.description: The sum of what the batch's items cost. Only successful items are charged.

webhook.description: Whether results go to a webhook.

index.description: The item's place in the batch's items, from 0.

request_id.description: The item's request, readable at GET /v1/fetch/{id}, once it has started.

error.description: Why the item failed without starting (refused before anything was sent; not charged). A fetch that ran and failed has its error in result.error.

result.description: The finished item's result (without the body; download it from /v1/fetch/{id}/content), or null while it is queued or running, or with results=false.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as cursor for the next page. With order=finished it is also how to read only what finished since: it stays set while the batch can still change, and is null once the batch is over and everything was read.

CaptureSettings.description: What to record. Every field is optional.

types.description: Which calls to record. Images, media, fonts, stylesheets, manifests and beacons are never recorded.

max_requests.description: Calls past this are counted in network.dropped.over_limit, not stored, and network.truncated is true.

max_body_bytes.description: Per response body. A longer body is cut and marked body_truncated. At most 25 MB of bodies are stored per request; later calls keep their headers and sizes, with body_omitted capture_full.

bodies.description: text: store bodies that are JSON, HTML, XML, plain text, JavaScript, GraphQL or form data. none: headers and sizes only. all: binary bodies too, as base64.

first_party_only.description: Keep only calls to the page's own registrable domain (example.com and *.example.com). Others are counted in network.dropped.third_party.

include_trackers.description: Keep calls to known analytics, advertising, tag manager and consent hosts, flagged tracker. By default they are dropped and counted in network.dropped.trackers.

unmask.description: Store and return secret header values in full instead of masked (see the headers of a call).

NetworkSummary.description: A request made with capture: how many calls were recorded and where to read them.

dropped.description: Calls seen and not stored, by reason.

truncated.description: max_requests was reached: later calls were counted, not stored.

attempt.description: The attempt (1 is the first entry of attempts) whose browser recorded these calls; null when no browser ran.

complete.description: false when the browser stopped (a deadline, a crash) before it reported everything: the calls it sent before are kept.

expires_at.description: When the calls are deleted with the rest of the content.

expired.description: true after DELETE: the calls are gone.

index.description: The call number, from 1 in the order the page made the calls.

page.description: 1 for the first page, 2 for the first POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next, and so on.

phase.description: warmup: FetchX's own visit to the site's home page before the page (protected sites); load: the page loading; scroll: after scrolling started; replay: FetchX getting back to the earlier page on a next page; actions: while the caller's actions ran.

status.description: Null when no response came (see error).

response_bytes.description: Bytes received for the body, as transferred.

first_party.description: Whether the call went to the page's own registrable domain.

started_ms.description: When the call started, in ms from the start of the page's load (warm-up calls are negative).

body_omitted.description: Why a response body was not stored: not_text (capture.bodies text), bodies_none, capture_full (25 MB per request reached) or unavailable (the browser no longer had it).

error.description: Why a call got no response: refused:<reason> when FetchX refused it (refused:resource_blocked, refused:request_limit), a browser error such as browser_err_aborted, or not_finished when it was still open at the end.

matched.description: With contains: the values this call's response body holds.

action_index.description: The caller's action that set the call off (see ActionResponse.action_index_started), or null.

complete.description: Whether the call finished: false when it failed or was still open when the page was read.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page of calls.

headers.description: Name and value pairs in the order sent, so repeated headers survive. Cookie, Set-Cookie, Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and any header whose name contains token, secret, api-key, session, password or credential show `<masked len=N sha=XXXXXX>` instead of the value (a cookie keeps its name), unless the request was made with capture.unmask.

body.description: Decompressed. Text bodies as UTF-8; binary ones (capture.bodies all) as base64. Null when not stored, or over 1 MB (see body_url).

body_omitted.description: Why a response body was not stored: not_text (capture.bodies text), bodies_none, capture_full (25 MB per request reached) or unavailable (the browser no longer had it).

body_url.description: For a body over 1 MB: /v1/fetch/{id}/network/{index}/body, read with the same key.

response.description: Null when no response came (see error).

redirected_from.description: The index of the call this one is a redirect of.

action_index.description: The caller's action that set the call off (see ActionResponse.action_index_started), or null.

complete.description: Whether the call finished: false when it failed or was still open when the page was read.

Me.description: The project and API key making the call.

project_id.description: The project. It stays the same when a key is rotated or replaced, so use it to recognise the customer.

key_id.description: This key. Rotating a key makes a new key_id. Null for a key set in the server configuration.

key_name.description: The name given to the key in the console.

key_prefix.description: The first characters of the key (fxk_ and 8 more), as the console shows them.

scopes.description: What this key may call: fetch:write (POST /v1/fetch, next pages, batches, estimates), fetch:read (results, content, network captures, DELETE) and usage:read (balance and usage).

limits.description: The limits set on this key in the console. Null fields have no limit, and all are null for a key from the server configuration.

expires_at.description: When the key stops working; after it, calls answer 401 api_key_expired.

concurrency.description: The project's concurrency limit. requests: how many of the project's requests may run at once, of any kind (HTTP or browser, next pages and batch items included), and how many are running now. Past it, POST /v1/fetch and POST /v1/fetch/{id}/next answer 429 too_many_requests with error.details.limit "requests". There is no separate limit for browser requests. A running batch leaves one of them free for single requests. Ask FetchX support to raise it. browser_sessions: how many browser sessions (POST /v1/browser-sessions) may be open at once, and how many are; an open session also counts as a running request.

limit.description: Requests that may run at once.

browser_sessions.description: Browser sessions the project may have open at once, and how many are open now. Past it, POST /v1/browser-sessions answers 429 too_many_requests with error.details.limit "browser_sessions". An open session also counts as a running request.

features.description: What this FetchX supports, by feature id, so a client can check before relying on a newer feature: actions (browser actions on POST /v1/fetch), allow_hosts (the host allowlist on POST /v1/fetch), batches, browser_sessions (POST /v1/browser-sessions), capture (network capture), capture_actions (wait_for_response, and action_index and complete on captured calls), estimate, extract, feedback, fixtures (FetchX's public test site, https://fixtures.fetchx.ai, may be fetched), key_limits (credit limits and expiry on keys), limits (concurrency in GET /v1/me), logins (saved site logins: /v1/logins, and login on POST /v1/fetch), next_page, redirect_manual (redirect: manual and all_headers on POST /v1/fetch), usd (USD prices in GET /v1/balance and GET /v1/prices). Ids are added as features ship, and are listed in the changelog; one is removed only after a deprecation.

KeyLimit.description: One of the key's credit limits and where the key stands against it now.

limit.description: Credits the key may spend in the period.

used.description: Credits its requests were charged in the period, plus what its running requests hold. A request counts in the period it started; requests made with the keys this one was rotated from count too.

remaining.description: limit minus used, at least 0. A request reserves at most this much.

resets_at.description: When the period ends: the next midnight UTC, or the first of next month UTC.

FeedbackRequest.description: A report about one request: give fetch_id (one of your requests, kept 90 days) or url, not both.

fetch_id.description: The request the report is about. FetchX keeps a copy of what it did with it, so the report stays useful after the result expires.

url.description: The page, when there is no request to name: an http or https URL.

kind.description: What you saw. blocked_via_fetchx_ok_from_home: the request failed or was walled through FetchX and works from your own connection. wrong_content: FetchX returned a page that is not the one you see (a different, empty or challenge page). extract_wrong: extract returned wrong or missing fields. other: anything else; say what in message.

evidence.description: Optional: what the request returned where it worked. Leave out secrets and personal data; FetchX staff read it.

body_excerpt.description: A short part of the body you got, such as the title or the data you expected.

client.description: Where and how it worked, for example "curl 8.5 from a home connection in DE".

Feedback.description: A report and where it stands.

kind.description: What you saw. blocked_via_fetchx_ok_from_home: the request failed or was walled through FetchX and works from your own connection. wrong_content: FetchX returned a page that is not the one you see (a different, empty or challenge page). extract_wrong: extract returned wrong or missing fields. other: anything else; say what in message.

url.description: The page: the request's URL when the report names fetch_id.

method.description: The method; null for a report that names fetch_id.

evidence.description: Optional: what the request returned where it worked. Leave out secrets and personal data; FetchX staff read it.

body_excerpt.description: A short part of the body you got, such as the title or the data you expected.

client.description: Where and how it worked, for example "curl 8.5 from a home connection in DE".

status.description: received: not looked at yet. reviewing: FetchX staff are on it. resolved: changed or explained (see reply). dismissed: nothing to change (see reply).

reply.description: FetchX staff's answer, when there is one.

JsonSkeleton.description: The shape of a JSON body (formats: skeleton), a few KB however large the body. Fields are read from the first 100 elements of each array. A JSON document a browser shows inside a lone <pre> is read from there.

root.description: The type of the whole document.

fields.description: Each path once, in the order first seen.

path.description: JSONPath: $ for the document, $.items for a key, $.items[*].price for a key of each element, $['a.b'] for a key that needs quoting.

type.description: object, array, string, number, boolean or null; several joined with | when it varies (string|null).

seen.description: How many times the path was seen: compare with the parent array's items to spot optional keys.

items.description: For an array: elements across every time it was seen.

sample.description: The body with every array cut to its first element and long strings cut short (null when even that is too large).

truncated.description: Fields past 150, or deeper or longer than the limits, were left out, or the sample was cut further to fit.

credits.description: The price of a successful request that this step got.

residential.description: The step goes out through a residential IP.

browser.description: The step loads the page in a browser.

route_classes.description: The route classes (route.class on a request) this step's price covers.

included_mb.description: Traffic included in the step's price, in MB; each started MB past it costs traffic.credits_per_mb. Null: traffic is not charged on this step.

Prices.description: FetchX's price table, in credits, and the credit packs that buy them.

steps.description: Each step auto mode can climb through, cheapest first. A request is charged for the step that got the data, never for the ones before it.

browser_sessions.description: Browser sessions (POST /v1/browser-sessions): a flat price per session, charged once when it ends (not when its browser failed), plus residential traffic past included_mb at traffic.credits_per_mb.

credits.description: Added for each captcha solved on a browser step that succeeded.

credits_per_mb.description: Added per started MB of residential traffic past the step's included_mb. block_resources (on by default) keeps most pages inside it.

extract.description: Reading a page into JSON with extract: credits per started unit of page text read, at least one unit.

unit_tokens.description: Tokens of page text in one unit (a token is about 4 characters).

max_tokens.description: The most page text read; text past it is not read or charged.

max_credits.description: The most extraction adds to one page.

packs.description: The credit packs on sale, smallest first. Credits never expire; a project's balance holds whatever it bought, in either currency.

usd.description: Price in USD, by card. Null when not sold in USD.

inr.description: Price in INR, by UPI. Null when not sold in INR.

trial_credits.description: Trial credits a new account gets once, on its first project. They share one balance with purchased credits and pay for every step. Null when this server grants none.

pricing_url.description: Credit packs and their prices in your currency.

ActionFrame.description: The frame to act in (default: the top frame): the first whose URL contains url_contains, or the iframe element selector matches. Waited for within the action's timeout; none gives frame_not_found.

Action.description: One step. Each type takes only its own fields (anything else is refused, invalid_request with details.field actions[i].name). Every action takes frame (not navigate, wait_for_url or wait_for_response), optional (a failed optional action does not stop the others) and timeout_ms (1 to 60000; an evaluate up to the request's timeout_ms). wait: ms (0 to 60000), or selector with state (attached, visible (default), hidden, detached). wait_for_url: url_contains or url_regex, matched against the top frame's URL. click: selector, button (left, right, middle), click_count (1 to 3); scrolls the element into view and waits until it can be clicked. hover: selector. fill: selector (default: the element with the focus, through open shadow roots) and value (up to 64 KB); clears the field and sets the value as typing would (input and change events). fill_secret: as fill, with secret, the name of an entry in the request's secrets; it is typed only into a field whose frame is at one of the secret's origins, over https (else the action fails with secret_origin_mismatch or secret_insecure). press: key (Enter, Tab, Control+a...), selector optional. select: selector and value or label. scroll: to (top, bottom) or px. navigate: url (https; on allow_hosts when given), in the same tab. evaluate: script (up to 64 KB) run in the page's own world; mode expression (default) gives the completion value of the script, as a console does, and function runs it as a function body with args (JSON up to 64 KB) and gives what it returns. A promise is awaited; the value comes back as JSON (up to 1 MB) in data.actions[i].value. A script that sends the page elsewhere ends ok with value null, and the next action runs in the new document. wait_for_response: url_contains or url_regex, method, status_in (HTTP statuses) and body (text (default) or none); matches the first response, as the browser's network layer saw it, to a request that started after the previous action began (any, for the first action) and that completes, and returns it in data.actions[i].response. type: text typed one key at a time, selector optional, delay_ms (0 to 1000) between keys.

args.description: Any JSON value, only with mode function: the function's args.

ActionResponse.description: The response a wait_for_response matched, from the browser's network layer (not the page's JavaScript): the exact request URL with its query, and the real HTTP status.

request_index.description: Its index in the network capture, when the request has capture and recorded it.

headers.description: Lowercased names; Cookie, Set-Cookie, Authorization and secret-named headers masked as in a capture.

body.description: With body text: the body, utf-8 text for text types, else base64; up to 2 MB (8 MB for all of a request's action results). null with body none, or for a response without one.

complete.description: Whether the whole body was read.

truncated.description: Whether body holds less than the whole body.

sha256.description: Of the whole body. null when one of the request's secrets was taken out of it.

action_index_started.description: The action that set the request off: the one running when it started, or, when that was a wait, the action before it.

status.description: skipped: an earlier action that was not optional failed, or the page did not answer 2xx.

value.description: evaluate only: the script's result as JSON.

message.description: What went wrong, with the failing selector at most; for evaluate_error, the script's own error. page_not_ok: the page answered other than 2xx, so no action ran.

type.description: What the request was: a browser resource type (document, script, xhr, fetch...), connection (a socket, worker or redirect hop the relay refused) or redirect (an HTTP redirect).

action_index.description: The action that set it off, or null.

Login.description: A saved site login. The password is never returned, and the username only masked.

site.description: The host FetchX may sign in on, such as login.example.com: the login is typed only into sign-in forms on this host and its subdomains, over https. A URL is taken as its host. It applies by itself to requests on the same registrable domain (a login for login.example.com serves requests to app.example.com); name it with the request’s `login` when the sign-in is on another domain (an SSO provider).

status.description: new: not used yet. signed_in: FetchX signed in with it and keeps the session. rejected: the site showed its sign-in form again after FetchX sent the login (a wrong password or unknown user), or three sign-ins in a row got no clear answer. code_required: after the password the site asked for a one-time code, which FetchX cannot give. FetchX does not type a rejected or code_required login again until you update it, since repeated wrong passwords can lock an account.

signed_in.description: Whether FetchX holds a signed-in session for it. Requests use the session first and sign in again only when the site asks.

last_sign_in.description: The last time FetchX sent the login, and how it went.

items.description: The project’s saved logins, oldest first (at most 50).

site.description: The host FetchX may sign in on, such as login.example.com: the login is typed only into sign-in forms on this host and its subdomains, over https. A URL is taken as its host. It applies by itself to requests on the same registrable domain (a login for login.example.com serves requests to app.example.com); name it with the request’s `login` when the sign-in is on another domain (an SSO provider).

password.description: Stored encrypted; never returned or logged, and taken out of stored pages and network captures.

LoginUpdate.description: A new site, username or password starts over: the saved session is dropped and the status is new again. A new name changes nothing else.

allow_hosts.description: The only hosts the session's browser may reach: exact hostnames, or *.suffix for every subdomain of suffix (not suffix itself). Every request a page or a frame makes (cross-origin frames included), every request its workers make and every connection (WebSockets included) is held to it: one to a host off the list is refused before it leaves FetchX and listed in blocked_requests. Captcha widgets load from their vendors' hosts, so list those for a page that shows one.

ttl_s.description: How long the session may run, counted from when it opens.

idle_ttl_s.description: The session closes when your connected client sends nothing for this long (idle), or when no client is connected for this long (disconnect).

route.description: The exit, one IP for the whole session: datacenter (the default) or residential, in country (US when left out).

value.description: The secret, 4 characters to 4096 bytes. FetchX never stores, logs or returns it: it is held in memory while the request runs, and wherever a page shows or echoes it (as typed, URL-encoded, form-encoded, JSON-escaped or base64) it comes back as [REDACTED:<name>].

origins.description: The https origins (scheme, host and port, no path), such as https://login.example.com, the secret may be typed into or sent to. Each host must be in allow_hosts.

secrets.description: The session's own secrets by name (1 to 8), each typed only into pages at the origins it names (each origin's host must be on allow_hosts), with POST /v1/browser-sessions/{id}/fill. A secret never reaches your client: from the start it is taken out of everything the session sends you (as [REDACTED:<name>]) in the forms a page may show or send it (as typed, URL-encoded, form-encoded, JSON-escaped, base64), and a request a page makes that carries it to another origin is stopped and named in secret_egress. FetchX keeps their names and origins only.

login.description: A saved login (POST /v1/logins) whose site is on allow_hosts. Its signed-in session's cookies are in the browser from the start, and POST /v1/browser-sessions/{id}/fill types its username and password (login.username, login.password) on its site's pages; the password never reaches your client.

viewport.description: The pages' viewport; left out, the browser identity's own.

max_credits.description: The most the session may cost. On a residential route it sets how much traffic the session may move (the included MB, then credits per MB, see GET /v1/prices); when it has moved that much it closes with close_reason traffic_limit. Left out, FetchX holds the session's price plus its default traffic allowance, and charges what the session used.

idempotency_key.description: The same key with the same body answers with the session it started (200), whatever state it is in now, and starts and charges nothing more; with another body it is refused (409 idempotency_conflict). Secret values are not compared, since FetchX keeps no trace of them. Use it so a create retried after a lost answer cannot start a second session.

BrowserSessionCredits.description: charged = step_credits + traffic_credits, capped at max.

traffic_mb.description: Megabytes (10^6 bytes) the session moved through its exit, to one decimal.

included_mb.description: Traffic included in a residential session's price; null when traffic is not charged.

traffic_credits.description: Per started MB past included_mb, on a residential route.

BrowserSession.description: A browser session; once closed, its receipt (kept for 90 days).

status.description: open: connect to ws_url. closed: the session has ended; this is its receipt.

expires_at.description: ready_at plus ttl_s: when it closes at the latest.

close_reason.description: client: closed with DELETE. ttl: reached ttl_s. idle: your client sent nothing for idle_ttl_s. disconnect: no client was connected for idle_ttl_s. traffic_limit: it moved what max_credits (or the default allowance) allows. error: its browser failed or did not start (not charged).

ws_url.description: Where your Playwright connects, over wss on port 443, with an API key of the project that has fetch:write in the Authorization header: playwright.firefox.connect(ws_url, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer fxk_...'}). The URL alone is useless without the key. Use the Playwright release in playwright.version (any patch of playwright.client); another one is refused with HTTP 428. Drive browser.contexts[0], the session's one context, and open pages in it with new_page(). New contexts, closing the browser or the context, launching browsers, tracing, screencasts, CDP and files on FetchX's side are refused with an error your client raises (counted in refused_calls); upload files from your side (set_input_files with a path or a buffer) and save downloads on your side. A client may disconnect and connect again while the session is open; up to 4 at once.

playwright.description: The Playwright release the session runs. A new release is announced in the changelog at least 14 days before sessions move to it.

client.description: The major.minor your client must have, such as 1.62.

browser.description: The browser: Camoufox, a hardened Firefox (connect with playwright.firefox).

duration_s.description: How long it has been open (until closed_at once closed).

traffic_mb.description: Megabytes (10^6 bytes) moved through its exit, both ways, to one decimal.

requests.description: Requests and connections FetchX let through.

connections.description: Client connections over the session; null while it is open.

blocked_requests.description: What FetchX refused, by origin and type (each pair once, at most 100; action_index is always null): requests to hosts off allow_hosts or to private addresses, websocket for a WebSocket a page tried to open off the list (wss:// origin), connection for a worker's request, socket or redirect hop the proxy refused.

opened.description: WebSockets the pages opened to hosts on allow_hosts.

refused.description: WebSockets to hosts off the list, refused and listed in blocked_requests.

secrets_used.description: Secrets typed into the session, by name.

secret_egress.description: Secrets a page tried to send to another origin; those requests were stopped.

refused_calls.description: Playwright calls the session refused your client, by Interface.method (such as Browser.newContext), with counts.

max.description: What was held for the session when it started: the most it can cost.

charged.description: What it cost: 0 while it is open, and for a session that ended in error.

error.description: With close_reason error: a code, such as browser_failed.

idempotency_key.description: The create's idempotency_key, if it had one.

secret.description: One of the session's secrets, or login.username / login.password of its saved login.

selector.description: A Playwright selector; the first element it matches is filled.

frame_url.description: The start of the https URL of the frame the field is in (for a field in a frame from another origin); the newest page's main frame when left out.
The frame it was typed in, without query or fragment.
